summary: The frontend is 4 files: src/main.ts (~4890 lines, entire UI as innerHTML-rendered vanilla TS into <div id="app"> from a minimal index.html), src/platform.ts (transport abstraction), src/updater.ts (Tauri-only auto-update), src/style.css (3745 lines, 3 cascading theme layers). Transport: platform.ts exports invoke()/listen() that mirror Tauri's API. Mode detection: isTauriRuntime() checks "__TAURI_INTERNALS__" in window; isRemoteMode() is true when not in Tauri, OR localStorage "codex-switch-terminal.remote.enabled"==="1", OR VITE_CST_API_BASE_URL is set — so a Tauri desktop build can also run in remote mode (boot calls tauriInvoke("client_startup_config") which can force remoteMode+baseUrl+token). In Tauri mode, invoke/listen pass straight through to @tauri-apps/api. In remote mode, remoteInvoke() maps each command name to a REST call on the cst-server (Bearer token auth, JSON; 401 on primary base clears the token and drops back to renderRemoteLogin). Events in remote mode come from an in-memory listeners Map fed by emit(); only two events exist: "pty-data" {id,data} and "pty-exit" {id}. Terminal I/O in remote mode uses one WebSocket per terminal at ws(s)://<node>/ws/terminals/:id?token=…; client sends {type:"input"|"resize"|"stop"}, server sends {type:"data"|"exit"|"error"|"status"|"pong"}; "status" is deliberately ignored (injecting text corrupts the Codex TUI redraw) and there is no reconnect on close — REST fallbacks (POST /api/terminals/:id/write|/resize, DELETE /api/terminals/:id) only cover writes. Multi-node routing: parseRemoteNodes() reads "label|baseUrl|token|priority" lines from localStorage/VITE_CST_REMOTE_NODES, health-checks GET /api/health (1200ms timeout), scores activeTerminals/capacity + priority/100, honors draining/ready flags, then tries POST /api/terminals on each candidate until one succeeds. An optional Android bridge (window.CstAndroid) seeds baseUrl/token. xterm sessions: createTerminalSession builds a Terminal+FitAddon per session; terminal.onData → invoke("write_terminal"); mountActiveTerminal swaps terminal.element into #terminal; render() rebuilds app.innerHTML wholesale (a guard skips render while the Kombai iframe runs). style.css layers: base warm-dark hardcoded palette (1–1764), a light "reference-inspired" layer introducing CSS tokens (--app-bg/--panel/--line/--text/--muted/--accent/--success/--warning/--danger/--info/--radius) (1766–3002), and the active "EVENT HORIZON" black theme (3003+) that re-defines :root tokens plus --accent-ink/--eh-glow/--font-head/--font-body/--font-mono; theme is fixed by cascade order, no data-theme toggle or prefers-color-scheme switching.
keyFacts: Transport is fully abstracted in src/platform.ts: same invoke(command,args)/listen(event,handler) signatures work in Tauri IPC and browser/WS mode — a chat UI built on these two functions works in both runtimes for free.

Complete invoke command list used by the frontend (34): load_settings, save_settings, ensure_account_home, import_account_json, import_account_docs (desktop-only), remove_account, account_limit_status, usage_dashboard, account_token_usage, pool_status, pool_start, pool_stop, pool_pick_terminal_account, start_terminal, list_dir, write_terminal, resize_terminal, stop_terminal, pick_project_dir (remote returns null), kombai_status, kombai_start, kombai_stop, kombai_install_extension, launch_ide (desktop-only), list_discussions, list_prompt_history (remote stubbed empty), claim_session_for_terminal, copy_discussion_to_account, delete_discussion, room_status, room_messages, room_send, room_enable/room_disable (remote no-ops), client_startup_config (Tauri-only, called via raw tauriInvoke in initializePlatform).
Only two events exist app-wide: pty-data {id:number,data:string} (raw ANSI bytes) and pty-exit {id:number}; subscribed once in setupEvents() (main.ts ~4746) and dispatched to sessions by ptyId.

Remote REST mapping (cst-server): GET/PUT /api/settings, POST /api/accounts/home|import, DELETE /api/accounts/:id, GET /api/limits|/api/usage|/api/account-usage, GET/POST /api/pool/*, POST /api/terminals (+ per-terminal write/resize/DELETE), GET /api/fs/list, /api/kombai/*, GET /api/discussions, POST /api/discussions/claim|copy|delete, GET /api/room/status|messages, POST /api/room/send, GET /api/health per node.

WS protocol per terminal: URL ws(s)://<node>/ws/terminals/:id?token=<token>. Client->server: {type:'input',data}, {type:'resize',cols,rows}, {type:'stop'}. Server->client: {type:'data',id,data}, {type:'exit',id}, {type:'error',id,message}, {type:'status',id,status,workspaceId,workspacePath} (intentionally dropped), {type:'pong',id} (client never pings, message unhandled).

start_terminal args differ by mode (main.ts ~4627): remote sends repoUrl+workspacePath, desktop sends projectDir; frontend pre-reserves the pty id (reservePtyId) and passes it as `id`; also cols/rows/command/agentId/branch.

The Agent Room is an existing chat-message precedent: room_messages {since} returns {messages: RoomMessage[], cursor:number} via polling — a pattern reusable for a chat pane; styles already exist ('Salon d'agents' sections at style.css 2700 and 3640).

Structured conversation data already exists server/backend-side via discussions (list_discussions, claim_session_for_terminal links a live terminal to its Codex session id) — a far better source for chat bubbles than parsing the ANSI PTY stream.

render() rebuilds the entire #app innerHTML on every state change (no vdom); xterm instances survive because their DOM element is detached/reattached in mountActiveTerminal(); Kombai iframe requires an explicit no-render guard — a chat UI needs the same detach/reattach or incremental-update treatment.

style.css theming: tokens are defined by three successive :root blocks; the LAST one (Event Horizon, line 3017) wins — there is no light/dark toggle, no data-theme attribute, no prefers-color-scheme theme switch; new chat CSS should consume the existing custom properties (--panel, --line, --text, --muted, --accent, --accent-ink, --radius, --eh-glow, --font-head/body/mono).

Layout skeleton: .layout is a 2-col grid (sidebar 260-300px | main); main column = .workspace with .topbar, .terminal-shell (grid rows: .terminal-tabs auto + #terminal 1fr), .settings-strip, .statusbar; breakpoints at 980px/680px; Event Horizon layer floats .layout in a translucent shell over a fixed .eh-bg (accretion-disk animation) injected by main.ts outside #app.

localStorage keys: codex-switch-terminal.remote.enabled|remote.base-url|remote.token|remote.nodes; env: VITE_CST_API_BASE_URL, VITE_CST_REMOTE_NODES; Android WebView bridge window.CstAndroid {getBaseUrl,getToken,setConfig,openSettings}.

updater.ts is desktop-only (checks __TAURI_INTERNALS__), uses @tauri-apps/plugin-updater check()/downloadAndInstall() + plugin-process relaunch(), gated by window.confirm; fired fire-and-forget from boot().
index.html is an empty shell: <div id="app"> + /src/main.ts module, lang=fr; all DOM including #terminal is generated in main.ts render(); UI copy is French.

sendLine() (main.ts ~4689) shows how prompts are already injected into the live Codex TUI: invoke('write_terminal', {id, data: line + '\r'}) — the existing 'Skill' buttons use it; a chat input box could ship text the same way as a first iteration.

Agent Room 3640, #terminal host 3706, modals 3713).
integrationPoints: listen('pty-data', {id,data}) / listen('pty-exit', {id}) in main.ts setupEvents (~4746) — the single output stream a chat renderer would tap or replace; in remote mode it is synthesized from the per-terminal WebSocket in platform.ts openTerminalSocket().
invoke('write_terminal', {id, data}) and sendLine(line) (main.ts ~4689) — the input path; a chat input box can inject prompts into the running Codex TUI exactly like the existing Skill buttons do.
invoke('start_terminal', {...}) / 'stop_terminal' / 'resize_terminal' — session lifecycle; frontend reserves the pty id up front (reservePtyId), so ids are known before the backend responds.

#terminal div inside .terminal-shell (built in render(), styled at style.css 850 & 3707) — the DOM slot a chat pane would replace or sit beside; .terminal-shell is a 2-row grid (tabs + host) ready to accept a third row or a split.

WS endpoint /ws/terminals/:id?token= with message types input/resize/stop (up) and data/exit/error/status/pong (down) — a chat transport could add new message types here, or add a parallel WS channel; note the unused 'status' and 'pong' types show the protocol is extensible.
remoteInvoke() switch in platform.ts (~211) — the one place to register any new command's REST mapping for web mode; new backend commands only need a Tauri handler + one case here.

Agent Room plumbing: room_status / room_messages({since}) -> {messages,cursor} / room_send({text,to}) with polling loops in main.ts (~1312-1382) and existing chat-panel CSS (style.css 2700, 3640) — closest existing pattern to an OpenCode-style message list.

Discussions/session APIs: list_discussions, claim_session_for_terminal (links live terminal to Codex session id, main.ts ~689), copy/delete_discussion — the structured (JSONL-backed) conversation source for rendering real message history instead of parsing ANSI.
emit()/listeners Map in platform.ts (~577) — internal event bus in remote mode; new synthetic events (e.g. 'chat-message') can be emitted here and consumed through the same listen() facade.

render() in main.ts — full innerHTML rebuild + createIcons(lucide); any persistent chat DOM (scroll position, virtualized list, in-flight markdown) must be kept outside this rebuild or detached/reattached like xterm elements in mountActiveTerminal().

boot() sequence (initializePlatform -> load_settings -> setupEvents -> render -> restoreTerminals) and renderRemoteLogin() — where a chat view registers itself and where auth gating happens (hasRemoteAuth / 401 -> clearRemoteConfig).
risks: The only live data channel is raw ANSI PTY bytes (pty-data); Codex CLI is a full-screen TUI with cursor-addressed redraws, so parsing it into chat messages is unreliable — the codebase itself avoids injecting into the stream (WS 'status' messages are deliberately dropped, platform.ts ~532). A real chat UI likely needs a new backend channel (codex exec/proto JSON mode or tailing the session JSONL that discussions already read).

No WS reconnect: openTerminalSocket is called only at terminal start; on socket close the entry is deleted and output silently stops (REST fallback covers writes only). A chat UI depending on this stream needs reconnection/backfill logic.

render() rebuilds all of #app via innerHTML on nearly every state change; a chat message list will lose scroll/selection/DOM state unless detached-reattached like xterm or the render pipeline is made incremental (the Kombai iframe no-render guard shows this is already a known pain point).

Feature asymmetry between modes must be preserved: in remote mode list_prompt_history returns an empty stub, pick_project_dir returns null, import_account_docs and launch_ide throw — a chat UI must gate features on isRemoteMode() like existing code does.
start_terminal argument names differ by mode (repoUrl/workspacePath remote vs projectDir desktop); any chat-driven session creation must replicate this split (main.ts ~4627).

Theme system is cascade-order dependent (three :root blocks, last wins, no data-theme toggle); adding chat styles before line 3003 will be silently overridden by the Event Horizon layer — new CSS should go after it and use the tokens.
Google Fonts @import at style.css line 1 needs network; also markdown rendering libs would need bundling (no CDN at runtime in Tauri CSP contexts).
Auth edge: any 401 from the primary base URL wipes the stored token mid-session (apiAt ~350); a long-lived chat view must handle sudden logout/re-render to the login screen.

Multi-node routing means different terminals of one 'conversation' can live on different servers (remoteTerminalRoutes per id); a chat UI aggregating across sessions must route per-terminal, not to a single base URL.
French-language UI strings and error messages are hardcoded throughout main.ts/platform.ts; new chat surfaces should match (no i18n layer exists).
